The task: produce a JUnit 4 test file covering methods of TokeniserState enum. Need to extract public methods (including abstract read? Actually read is abstract and package-private? The enum has abstract void read(Tokeniser t, CharacterReader r); that's package-private (default) visibility, not public. But we can still test via invoking read on each enum constant using a mock Tokeniser and CharacterReader to see behavior. However we likely cannot instantiate real Tokeniser and CharacterReader (they are internal). For test we can create simple stub classes that extend/implement needed methods. Use Mockito to mock Tokeniser and CharacterReader. We'll need to import org.junit.*, org.mockito.*. We'll test a subset: e.g., Data.read, TagOpen.read, EndTagOpen.read, etc. Identify edge cases: nullChar, eof, unexpected chars, etc.

Since the class is package-private (default) enum, test class must be in same package org.jsoup.parser to access. We'll place test in same package.

We'll write tests using Mockito to verify interactions: e.g., for Data state when current is '&' should call t.advanceTransition(CharacterReferenceInData). etc.

Edge cases: Data state with nullChar should call t.error(this) and emit nullChar. EOF should emit EOF token.

Similarly TagOpen with letter should call t.createTagPending(true) and transition TagName.

TagOpen with non-letter should error, emit '<', transition Data.

EndTagOpen with empty reader should call t.eofError and emit "</" and transition Data.

TagName handling of various characters: after tag name, when char is '>' should emitTagPending and transition Data; when '/' should transition SelfClosingStartTag; whitespace should transition BeforeAttributeName; nullChar should append replacementStr; eof should error and transition Data.

We'll create a stub Tokeniser with methods: advanceTransition, error, emit(Object), transition(TokeniserState), createTagPending(boolean), createTagPending(false) etc. Use Mockito to verify calls.

Also need to test static helper methods like readData, readCharRef, readEndTag, handleDataEndTag, etc. They are private static, cannot directly call. But we can indirectly test via appropriate states.

Simplify: Provide tests for a few representative methods and edge cases.

We'll produce a single test file with multiple test methods.

Ensure JUnit 4 imports: org.junit.Test, org.junit.Before, org.junit.runner.RunWith, org.mockito.Mock, org.mockito.MockitoAnnotations, org.mockito.junit.MockitoJUnitRunner.

We'll use @RunWith(MockitoJUnitRunner.class) for mocks.

We'll create mock Tokeniser and CharacterReader.

For CharacterReader, need methods: current(), isEmpty(), matchesLetter(), matches(char), matchConsume(String), matchConsumeIgnoreCase(String), consume(), consumeData(), consumeToAny(...), etc. We'll stub using Mockito to return predetermined values.

We'll test Data.read:

- case '&' -> verify advanceTransition called with CharacterReferenceInData.

- case '<' -> verify advanceTransition(TagOpen).

- case nullChar -> verify error called with TokeniserState.Data, emit called with nullChar char.

- case eof -> verify emit called with instance of Token.EOF.

- default -> verify consumeData called, emit called with returned string.

We'll set up CharacterReader mock accordingly.

Similarly for TagOpen.read letter case.

Edge cases for TagOpen non-letter like '!' which should error, emit '<', transition Data.

We'll also test EndTagOpen empty reader: isEmpty true leads to eofError, emit("</"), transition Data.

We'll test TagName with '>' char.

We'll need to mock TokeniserState constants for transition parameter checking; we can verify transition called with expected enum constant.

Implementation details: When we call TokeniserState.Data.read(tokeniser, reader), the method uses 'this' inside error and transition calls; we need to verify that tokeniser.error(TokeniserState.Data) was called. Use verify(tokeniser).error(TokeniserState.Data);

Note that tokeniser.error expects TokeniserState argument; we can match any.

Now produce test file.
